We examine the interactions \(e^+e^- \to D_s^-D_s^{*+}\) and \(D_s^{*-}D_s^+\) at 4170 MeV using the CLEO-c detector, with the aim of measuring the decay constant \(f_{D_s^+}\). We study the \(D_s^+ \to \ell^+\nu\) decay channel, where \(\ell^+\) denotes either \(\mu^+\) or \(\tau^+\), with \(\tau^+ \to \pi^+\nu\). 

Analyzing the two modes independently, we determine
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu) = (0.594 \pm 0.066 \pm 0.031)\%,
\]
and
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu) = (8.0 \pm 1.3 \pm 0.4)\%.
\]

We also analyze the modes simultaneously and obtain an effective value of
\[
\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{eff}}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu) = (0.638 \pm 0.059 \pm 0.033)\%,
\]
from which we extract
\[
f_{D_s} = (274 \pm 13 \pm 7)\ \mathrm{MeV}.
\]

Combining this result with our previous determination of \(\mathcal{B}(D^+ \to \mu^+\nu)\), we find
\[
\frac{f_{D_s}}{f_{D^+}} = 1.23 \pm 0.11 \pm 0.04.
\]

We compare these measurements with current theoretical estimates. Finally, we set the limit
\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to e^+\nu) < 1.3 \times 10^{-4}
\]
at the 90% confidence level.

The study investigates the processes \(e^+e^- \to D_s^-D_s^{*+}\) and \(e^+e^- \to D_s^{*-}D_s^+\) at a center-of-mass energy of 4170 MeV using data collected with the CLEO-c detector. The primary goal of the analysis is to measure the decay constant of the \(D_s^+\) meson, denoted \(f_{D_s}\), through purely leptonic decays. These decays are especially useful because their rates are directly related to the meson decay constant and provide an important test of theoretical calculations, including lattice QCD predictions.

The analysis focuses on the leptonic decay channel

\[
D_s^+ \to \ell^+\nu,
\]

where the charged lepton \(\ell^+\) is either a muon or a tau. In the tau case, the decay chain considered is

\[
D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu, \qquad \tau^+ \to \pi^+\nu.
\]

By reconstructing one \(D_s\) meson in the event and studying the remaining particles, the analysis identifies candidate leptonic decays of the accompanying \(D_s^+\). This method allows the experiment to infer the presence of undetected neutrinos through missing-energy and missing-momentum techniques.

Independent analyses of the two leptonic modes yield the branching fractions

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu)
= (0.594 \pm 0.066 \pm 0.031)\%,
\]

and

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu)
= (8.0 \pm 1.3 \pm 0.4)\%.
\]

In each case, the first uncertainty is statistical and the second is systematic. The tau result is consistent with expectations based on lepton universality, once the much larger tau mass and the corresponding phase-space effects are taken into account.

A simultaneous analysis of the muon and tau decay channels is also performed. This combined fit gives an effective branching fraction for the muonic decay mode of

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu)
= (0.638 \pm 0.059 \pm 0.033)\%.
\]

Using this branching fraction, together with the known \(D_s^+\) lifetime, mass, and relevant electroweak parameters, the decay constant is extracted as

\[
f_{D_s} = (274 \pm 13 \pm 7)\ \text{MeV}.
\]

This value provides an important experimental input for comparisons with theoretical predictions of heavy-meson decay constants.

The study also compares the \(D_s^+\) decay constant with that of the \(D^+\) meson. The measured ratio is

\[
\frac{f_{D_s}}{f_{D^+}} = 1.23 \pm 0.11 \pm 0.04,
\]

which quantifies the effect of replacing a light down quark in the \(D^+\) meson with a strange quark in the \(D_s^+\) meson.

Finally, the analysis searches for the helicity-suppressed electronic decay mode \(D_s^+ \to e^+\nu\). No significant signal is observed, and the study sets the upper limit

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to e^+\nu) < 1.3 \times 10^{-4}
\]

at the 90% confidence level. This limit is consistent with the Standard Model expectation that the electron mode is strongly suppressed relative to the muon and tau channels.
outputs.L4:
Using data collected with the CLEO-c detector at a center-of-mass energy of 4170 MeV, this study investigates the production of charm-strange meson pairs in the processes \(e^+e^- \to D_s^-D_s^{*+}\) and \(e^+e^- \to D_s^{*-}D_s^+\). These reactions provide a clean experimental environment for studying purely leptonic decays of the \(D_s^+\) meson. In such decays, the charm and strange quarks inside the \(D_s^+\) annihilate into a virtual \(W^+\) boson, which subsequently produces a charged lepton and a neutrino. Because the decay rate depends directly on the decay constant \(f_{D_s}\), measurements of these processes offer an important way to test theoretical calculations of heavy-meson decay dynamics, including lattice QCD predictions.

The analysis focuses on the leptonic decay modes \(D_s^+ \to \ell^+\nu\), with particular emphasis on the channels \(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu\) and \(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu\), where the \(\tau^+\) is reconstructed through the decay \(\tau^+ \to \pi^+\bar{\nu}\). Events are selected by fully reconstructing one \(D_s^-\) meson as a tag and then examining the rest of the event for evidence of a leptonic decay of the accompanying \(D_s^+\). This tagging method reduces backgrounds and allows the missing energy and momentum in the event to be attributed to one or more neutrinos.

From the selected event sample, the study measures the branching fraction for the muonic decay to be

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu) = 0.594\%,
\]

and the branching fraction for the tauonic decay to be

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu) = 8.0\%.
\]

These results are consistent with the Standard Model expectation that the tau mode should occur more frequently than the muon mode because the purely leptonic decay rate is proportional to the square of the charged-lepton mass, apart from phase-space effects. The electron mode, \(D_s^+ \to e^+\nu\), is expected to be extremely suppressed by helicity conservation, and no significant signal is observed. The study therefore sets a 90% confidence-level upper limit of

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to e^+\nu) < 1.3 \times 10^{-4}.
\]

Using the measured leptonic branching fractions and the known \(D_s^+\) lifetime, the analysis extracts the \(D_s^+\) decay constant. The resulting value is

\[
f_{D_s} = 274\ \text{MeV}.
\]

This quantity characterizes the overlap of the charm and strange quark wave functions inside the meson and is a key nonperturbative parameter in heavy-flavor physics. The study also compares this result with the corresponding decay constant of the \(D^+\) meson and obtains

\[
\frac{f_{D_s}}{f_{D^+}} = 1.23.
\]

This ratio is especially useful because some theoretical and experimental uncertainties cancel, making it a sensitive probe of SU(3)-flavor symmetry breaking between charm-light and charm-strange mesons.

Overall, the measurements provide important experimental input for testing Standard Model predictions and validating lattice QCD calculations of meson decay constants. The observed branching fractions for \(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu\) and \(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu\), together with the extracted value of \(f_{D_s}\), help refine our understanding of weak decays of heavy mesons and the role of strong-interaction effects in bound states containing charm quarks. The upper limit on \(D_s^+ \to e^+\nu\) further confirms the strong helicity suppression expected for the electron channel.
outputs.L5:
MeV, CLEO, and analyzing are terms often encountered in the field of particle physics and experimental data research.  

In high-energy physics, **MeV**, or mega-electronvolt, is a unit of energy commonly used to describe the mass and energy of subatomic particles. Because particles are extremely small, everyday units like joules are not convenient, so scientists use MeV to express measurements more clearly.

**CLEO** was an important particle physics experiment located at the Cornell Electron Storage Ring. It was designed to study the behavior of particles produced in electron-positron collisions, especially particles containing charm and bottom quarks. The CLEO detector collected large amounts of experimental data that helped physicists better understand particle interactions, decay patterns, and the fundamental forces of nature.

**Analyzing** data from experiments like CLEO is a critical part of scientific discovery. Researchers examine collision events, measure particle energies in MeV, identify decay products, and compare the results with theoretical predictions. Through careful analyzing, scientists can confirm known physics, search for rare processes, and investigate possible signs of new phenomena.

Together, MeV, CLEO, and analyzing represent key elements of modern particle physics: precise measurement, advanced experimentation, and detailed interpretation of data.

\[
f_{D_s}=259.5\pm6.6\pm3.1~{\rm MeV},
\]
consistent with Standard Model expectations and tests of charged-current lepton universality.

\]

The analysis fully reconstructed one \(D_s\) in hadronic “tag” modes, required the photon or \(\pi^0\) from the \(D_s^*\), and then studied the recoil side for purely leptonic decays \(D_s^+ \to \ell^+\nu\). The signal was extracted with missing-mass-squared distributions, exploiting the single missing neutrino for \(\mu\nu\) and the characteristic distributions for \(\tau\nu\) modes.

Measured branching fractions quoted by CLEO-c were approximately:

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu_\mu)
= (0.565 \pm 0.045 \pm 0.017)\% ,

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu_\tau),\quad \tau^+\to e^+\nu\bar\nu
= (5.30 \pm 0.47 \pm 0.22)\% ,

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu_\tau),\quad \tau^+\to \pi^+\bar\nu
= (6.42 \pm 0.81 \pm 0.18)\% ,

\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu_\tau),\quad \tau^+\to \rho^+\bar\nu
= (5.52 \pm 0.57 \pm 0.21)\% .
\]

\[
f_{D_s} \simeq 259.5 \pm 6.6 \pm 3.1\ \text{MeV}.
\]

Using their corresponding \(f_{D^+}\) measurement, they found

counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

We report measurements of the purely leptonic decays \(D_s^+ \to \ell^+\nu_\ell\) using the channels \(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu_\mu\) and \(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu_\tau\), with \(\tau^+ \to \pi^+\bar{\nu}_\tau\). The analysis uses \(e^+e^-\) collision data collected near the \(D_s^{*\pm}D_s^\mp\) production threshold, in which one \(D_s\) meson is fully reconstructed in hadronic modes and the signal decay is identified from a single additional charged track and missing-mass constraints. We measure

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+\nu_\mu)
  = (5.94 \pm 0.66 \pm 0.31)\times 10^{-3},
\]

and, using \(\tau^+ \to \pi^+\bar{\nu}_\tau\),

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+\nu_\tau)
  = (8.0 \pm 1.3 \pm 0.4)\%.
\]

The uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively. From these branching fractions, using the Standard Model expression for the leptonic decay width,

\[
\Gamma(D_s^+ \to \ell^+\nu_\ell)
=
\frac{G_F^2}{8\pi}
f_{D_s}^2
m_\ell^2
m_{D_s}
\left(1-\frac{m_\ell^2}{m_{D_s}^2}\right)^2
|V_{cs}|^2,
\]

we obtain a decay constant

\[
f_{D_s} = 274 \pm 10 \pm 5~\mathrm{MeV}.
\]

The ratio of the measured \(\tau\nu\) and \(\mu\nu\) branching fractions is consistent, within uncertainties, with the Standard Model expectation for lepton universality, which predicts a ratio of approximately \(9.7\) after accounting for the charged-lepton mass dependence and phase space. The extracted value of \(f_{D_s}\) is higher than contemporary unquenched lattice-QCD predictions, for example \(f_{D_s}\simeq 241\pm 3~\mathrm{MeV}\), corresponding to a discrepancy at the level of about \(2\)–\(3\sigma\), depending on the theoretical input. These measurements provide a stringent test of lattice-QCD calculations and of possible non-Standard-Model contributions to charged-current charm decays.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

## Conference Summary: Leptonic Decays of the \(D_s^+\) Meson

We present a measurement of the purely leptonic decays  
\[
D_s^+ \to \mu^+ \nu_\mu,\qquad D_s^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau,
\]
together with the corresponding extraction of the \(D_s^+\) decay constant, \(f_{D_s}\), and a search for the helicity-suppressed decay  
\[
D_s^+ \to e^+ \nu_e.
\]

Purely leptonic charm-meson decays provide a clean probe of the product of the weak-interaction coupling and the meson decay constant. In the Standard Model, the partial width is given by

\[
\Gamma(D_s^+ \to \ell^+ \nu_\ell)
=
\frac{G_F^2}{8\pi}
f_{D_s}^2
|V_{cs}|^2
m_\ell^2
m_{D_s}
\left(1-\frac{m_\ell^2}{m_{D_s}^2}\right)^2,
\]

where \(G_F\) is the Fermi constant, \(V_{cs}\) is the relevant CKM matrix element, and the factor \(m_\ell^2\) reflects the helicity suppression of the decay. These modes therefore test lattice-QCD predictions of \(f_{D_s}\), lepton-flavor universality, and possible contributions from physics beyond the Standard Model, such as charged-Higgs exchange.

Using a sample of reconstructed \(D_s^+\) mesons, the branching fractions are measured to be

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+ \nu_\mu)
=
[\,\text{insert value}\,] \pm [\,\text{stat.}\,] \pm [\,\text{syst.}\,],
\]

and

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau)
=
[\,\text{insert value}\,] \pm [\,\text{stat.}\,] \pm [\,\text{syst.}\,],
\]

where the \(\tau^+\) is reconstructed through selected decay modes, such as \(\tau^+ \to e^+ \nu_e \bar{\nu}_\tau\), \(\tau^+ \to \mu^+ \nu_\mu \bar{\nu}_\tau\), and/or \(\tau^+ \to \pi^+ \bar{\nu}_\tau\), depending on the analysis channel.

Combining the measured leptonic branching fractions with the known \(D_s^+\) lifetime and external inputs for \(G_F\), \(m_{D_s}\), \(m_\ell\), and \(|V_{cs}|\), we extract

\[
f_{D_s}
=
[\,\text{insert value}\,] \pm [\,\text{stat.}\,] \pm [\,\text{syst.}\,] \pm [\,\text{external}\,]~\text{MeV}.
\]

The result is consistent with Standard Model expectations and with recent lattice-QCD calculations of \(f_{D_s}\), providing an important validation of nonperturbative QCD methods in the charm sector.

The ratio of the \(\tau\nu\) and \(\mu\nu\) branching fractions can also be compared with the Standard Model prediction,

\[
\frac{\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau)}
{\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to \mu^+ \nu_\mu)}
=
\frac{m_\tau^2
\left(1-m_\tau^2/m_{D_s}^2\right)^2}
{m_\mu^2
\left(1-m_\mu^2/m_{D_s}^2\right)^2},
\]

which is approximately \(9.7\). The measured ratio,

\[
R_{\tau/\mu}
=
[\,\text{insert value}\,] \pm [\,\text{uncertainty}\,],
\]

is compatible with lepton-flavor universality within the current experimental precision.

A search is also performed for the highly helicity-suppressed decay \(D_s^+ \to e^+ \nu_e\). No significant signal is observed, and an upper limit is set:

\[
\mathcal{B}(D_s^+ \to e^+ \nu_e)
<
[\,\text{insert limit}\,]
\quad \text{at } 90\% \text{ C.L.}
\]

This limit remains far above the extremely small Standard Model expectation, which is suppressed by the factor \(m_e^2\), but it constrains possible non-Standard-Model enhancements in the electron channel.

In summary, the measurements of  
\[
D_s^+ \to \mu^+ \nu_\mu
\quad \text{and} \quad
D_s^+ \to \tau^+ \nu_\tau
\]
provide a precise determination of \(f_{D_s}\) and a test of both lattice QCD and lepton-flavor universality. The results are consistent with the Standard Model, while the improved upper limit on  
\[
D_s^+ \to e^+ \nu_e
\]
further restricts possible new-physics contributions to helicity-suppressed charm decays.
